title: Tiberias
hookLine: he is buried in Tiberias, visited by many

lines: A CITY ON THE SEA OF GALILEE.
cards: A lake in the north of the land of Israel, the Sea of Galilee, with a city on its western shore. Fishing boats, a promenade, hot springs, heat that hangs over the water in summer.
And a short walk up from the shore, a tomb where people stop to pray, light candles and leave small stones. Maimonides died in Egypt. Yet this is where tradition says he rests.

teach.h: FROM EGYPT TO THE LAND OF ISRAEL.
teach.b: Tiberias. First, the journey. Maimonides died in Egypt, where he had worked as a doctor and led a community.
Tradition says his body was carried from there to the land of Israel and buried in Tiberias, and legends grew up around that journey.
Some readers see a wish behind it: to lie in the land whose laws fill so much of his code. Second, the stone over him.
You met his epitaph early in this block: from Moses to Moses there arose none like Moses.
Tradition links that saying to his grave, and places other great teachers buried nearby, so a walk through that part of the city passes through generations of learning. Third, what people do there.
They come to pray, to recite psalms, to light a candle.
Some leave a small stone on the grave. The reasons people give vary: a sign that someone visited, a marker that lasts longer than flowers, a way of saying the memory still stands.

Jewish teachers who speak about prayer at a grave often stress that the prayer is directed to God, sometimes asking for help in the merit of the righteous person buried there. Fourth, the blessing in a name.

teach.h: MAY HIS MEMORY BE A BLESSING.
teach.b: Proverbs says, "The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing."
That verse stands behind the words said after the name of someone who has died: zichrono livrachah, may his memory be a blessing. And so his name, too, is said with a blessing after it.

how: Jews visit the graves of family and of great teachers to pray and recite psalms, often leaving a small stone, and add 'may his memory be a blessing' when speaking of someone who has died.

games.q: you've come to Maimonides' grave in Tiberias, and you're about to leave. what is one custom visitors keep?
o: take a stone from the grave as a keepsake.
leave a small stone on the grave.
games.why: they leave a small stone, a sign that someone came and that the memory still stands.

practice: Bring to mind a teacher who has died, a grandparent, a rabbi, a coach, someone who taught you to do one thing well, and in your mind set a small stone where they rest.
Say their name and one thing they taught you; if you pray, you can add "the memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing."
If a loss ever feels too heavy to carry alone, please reach out: in the US, call or text 988, any hour; elsewhere, local emergency help.
